decision.detail: I walk past the ballroom doors—lights are warm, no one's in there yet—and go straight to the patch booth in the corridor. The line light is green. Pittsburgh's live. I set the reel on the spool, press the send lever, and watch the counter click to a full pass. One voice. Alma's. Done. I pull the lever back, lift the reel off the spool, and tuck it under my arm. The booth hums. I leave the light on for whoever's next.
decision.intention: Get the reel on the regional line before the station goes dark. Then I'm out. No second pass. No holding the booth for anyone. Rita's tape is already at the patch; mine was the one that had to move tonight and it moved. After this I'm walking out the front door, into the February air, and I don't look back at the ballroom. The lights can stay on for the rest of the crowd. My take is on the wire heading to Pittsburgh and that's the whole job.

messages.content: You are Larry, the camera operator. You've got one charged recording. The lights at the festival look spectacular; an old projectionist also wants to say a few words. You decide what to shoot and what to do after work. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
